proposed.seoTitle: Understand how X-ray inspection works in food production
proposed.seoDescription: See how an X-ray system detects dense contaminants in packaged food, what affects performance, and why results are confirmed on your own product and line.

proposed.seoTitle: X-ray or metal detection: how to choose for your product
proposed.seoDescription: Compare X-ray and metal detection by what you need to find, your packaging and line space, and see when each system or a combination fits.

proposed.seoTitle: Understand how metal detection works and when to use it
proposed.seoDescription: Metal detectors use a balanced coil system, and wet, salty or hot products can disturb the field. Test with your real contaminant types at line speed.

proposed.seoTitle: Checkweighing basics: keep fill weights compliant
proposed.seoDescription: A checkweigher compares each pack against a target weight and rejects packs outside the range, giving a record of under-filling and over-filling.

proposed.seoTitle: How to plan a combination inspection system for your line
proposed.seoDescription: Combination systems put X-ray, metal detection and checkweighing in one frame with a single reject, saving floor space and operator time.

proposed.seoTitle: How to Choose Reject Systems and Conveyors for Inspection Lines
proposed.seoDescription: The reject type depends on product shape, speed and how the failed pack must be handled. Compare pusher, air blast, drop flap and retracting belt options.

proposed.seoTitle: Prepare a product sample for inspection testing
proposed.seoDescription: Inspection performance depends on your real product and packaging. A good sample set makes the test meaningful.

proposed.seoTitle: How to read inspection sensitivity claims and product effect
proposed.seoDescription: Sensitivity depends on the contaminant, product, packaging and line speed. Ask for the test conditions behind any sensitivity claim and a test on your own product.

proposed.seoTitle: How to fit inspection equipment into an existing line
proposed.seoDescription: Space, product flow and reject handling usually decide the layout more than the inspection technology itself. Measure the space first, then choose the technology.

proposed.seoTitle: Prepare details before requesting an inspection quotation
proposed.seoDescription: A short, specific brief gets a more useful inspection quotation. Include product, pack format, contaminants, line speed, packaging and space.

proposed.seoTitle: Learn how X-ray inspection handles aluminium trays and foil
proposed.seoDescription: X-ray inspection is not blocked by aluminium trays, foil or metalised film. Packaging affects the image, so settings are confirmed against your actual pack.

proposed.seoTitle: Find out if you should send product samples for testing
proposed.seoDescription: A test with your real product in its final packaging gives a meaningful performance figure, while a different product or pack size can mislead.

proposed.seoTitle: Find out which metals a metal detector can detect
proposed.seoDescription: A standard metal detector finds ferrous, non-ferrous and stainless-steel contamination. Sensitivity depends on aperture size, the product and line speed.

proposed.seoTitle: Understand why wet products affect metal detection
proposed.seoDescription: Wet, salty or hot products can disturb the detector field, called product effect. See how phase discrimination compensates and why product testing matters.

proposed.seoTitle: Understand checkweigher accuracy on your line
proposed.seoDescription: Accuracy depends on pack weight relative to the weigh cell, belt speed, pack stability and vibration; confirm actual results on your line.

proposed.seoTitle: Understand How Checkweighers Reject Out-of-Weight Packs
proposed.seoDescription: A checkweigher compares each pack against the target range and activates a pusher, air blast, drop flap or other reject device for non-conforming packs.

proposed.seoTitle: See which food and packaging industries LITUBO serves
proposed.seoDescription: LITUBO serves bakery, meat and seafood, frozen food, bottled and canned products, powders and granules, and pharmaceutical or daily-chemical packs.

proposed.seoTitle: How to Inspect Frozen Products with X-ray and Metal Detection
proposed.seoDescription: Frozen products can be inspected, but ice crystals and product density affect X-ray and metal detection performance. Testing with frozen samples is recommended.

proposed.seoTitle: Request spare parts using your model and serial number
proposed.seoDescription: Send the machine model and serial number, plus the part description or a photo, through the spare-parts request form. We will confirm the correct part.

proposed.seoTitle: How to Arrange Operator Training for Inspection Equipment
proposed.seoDescription: Operator and maintenance training can be arranged as part of a project or as a separate service visit, with scope and schedule confirmed with your team.

proposed.seoTitle: How to Request a Replacement Manual for Your Machine
proposed.seoDescription: Manuals are supplied with the machine. To get a replacement copy, send the model and serial number through the support request form.

proposed.seoTitle: How to Get a Quotation for Inspection Equipment
proposed.seoDescription: Send product type, pack format, contaminants, line speed, packaging material and space constraints. Our team confirms the configuration before quoting.

proposed.seoTitle: Find Where LITUBO Is Based: Kunshan, Jiangsu, China
proposed.seoDescription: LITUBO operates under Shanghai NingPin Industrial Dev. Co., Ltd. in Kunshan, Jiangsu Province, China and works with distributors and end users internationally.

proposed.seoTitle: How to enquire about becoming an equipment distributor
proposed.seoDescription: We welcome enquiries from distributors. Use the become-a-partner form and tell us about your market, customers and technical support capability.
